correctness.rationale: For each nonfull part i, selected-neighbor count is d-d_i, so feasible iff d-d_i>=2. This proves the universal gamma2 dichotomy: 2 selected requires a complete 2-part or two 1-parts, otherwise 3 from distinct parts (r>=3); bipartite threshold follows by separately checking incomplete shores. For stability, an original small part must be deleted/shortened to remove 2-witnesses, whereas creating a 2-part from a big part costs m-2, or deleting the sole singleton in r=3 changes the surviving biclique. Lower/upper deletion bounds match in all branches incl. K_2,2 needing 3 and K_2,3 needing 1. Independent occupancy/deletion brute for 53 cases, some with repeated sizes, matched; the uniform occupancy proof supplies the infinite-size conclusion.
